WHAT THIS MODEL IS. The backend routing decision the deployed llm-d-sc/Praxis table actually makes: SIMPLE/MEDIUM -> the small model, COMPLEX/REASONING -> the large one. It is not a four-tier complexity classifier. A tier classifier saying MEDIUM where the jury said SIMPLE picks the same backend and has made no routing error; tier-exact accuracy charges it for one anyway. Folding a 4-way model's output onto this decision scores 88.22%; training it directly scores 93.35%.

THIS DECISION FIRES ON EVERY REQUEST, which is why it is worth a dedicated model even though its accuracy is the lowest of the four gates in this family.

READ THE BASELINE AND THE MINORITY CLASS. Majority baseline on refined gold is 80.59% (always answer SMALL). 93.35% clears it by 12.8 points, and LARGE recall is 91.78% on a class that is 19.4% of the eval -- the minority class is doing real work. LARGE precision is 77.91%, i.e. about 6% of small requests are over-routed to the large model. That is a cost trade, and the direction most deployments prefer to the reverse; move the threshold if yours does not.

WEAKEST POINT, STATED. On the 176 rows where the three-model jury SPLIT, it scores 77.84% against a 72.16% baseline -- clear of chance but 15 points below its clean-subset figure. Contested rows are about 30% of real traffic here.
